war_declared.text: {my_faction} has put its name to this war, and I trust the council will remember who argued for patience first.
So {enemy_faction} wants a war. The council sits tonight, and I will be the one holding the minutes.
Swords are drawn against {enemy_faction}. Funny how the loudest voices in the hall always find battle easiest to fund.
We are at war with {enemy_faction}. I hope the lords who voted for this have also budgeted for the grain.

peace_made.text: Terms agreed with {faction}. Some of our hot-headed barons will sulk for a season, but they will come round.
{my_faction} and {faction} have signed. Peace suits the merchants and the people, and happens to suit my ledgers too.
A truce with {faction} at last. The council will call it wisdom. I would call it a sensible delay.
The peace with {faction} is sealed. Credit to the few who kept talking when the rest of the hall wanted blood.

player_joined_my_faction.text: Welcome to {my_faction}, {player}. The hall is richer for your sword, and I have already drafted your seat.
{player} has sworn to {my_faction}. I am sure they will find the council's rules are not so dull once learned.
{player}, you have chosen well. Come find me after the next session and we shall discuss what you are owed.
{player}, the oath is taken. I shall be watching how you keep it, as the council will.

player_left_my_faction.text: {player} has gone over to {faction}. A pity. Some of us will remember the ones who run at the first better offer.
{player} has left {my_faction} for {faction}. Ambition is a fine thing, though it makes people forgetful of old friends.
{player}, I shall not pretend I am surprised. I simply wish you had told me before the rest of the hall heard it.
I bear you no grudge, {player}. Whatever {faction} promised, I hope it was written down.

player_granted_fief.text: {fief} has gone to {player}. Congratulations are in order, though I did wonder whether the council was asked.
{player} now holds {fief}. Generous of our ruler. I shall be curious how long the gift lasts.
{player}, {fief} is yours now. Enjoy it while the council is still polite about it.
{player}, {fief} suits you. A fine seat, and the lords will need someone to answer to. Let us talk about that.

whisper_alliance_offer.text: {player}, {rival} takes every lord's silence for consent. Care to join me against {enemy_faction} before they move?
{player}, I have a proposal for the two of us. {enemy_faction} is weaker than their speeches. Shall we speak tonight?
{player}, you and I would do well together against {enemy_faction}. Say the word and I will bring the papers.
{player}, I hear {rival} has been whispering about you in the hall. A quiet pact against {enemy_faction} might change that.

my_faction_took_fief.text: {fief} is ours. {enemy_faction} will mourn it in their own fashion, but the gates belong to {my_faction} now.
The banners of {my_faction} fly over {fief} at last. I am told {enemy_faction} took it rather badly.
{fief} has fallen to {my_faction}. A fine result for the council, and a small reminder to {enemy_faction} of what patience costs.
Good news from {fief}. {enemy_faction} lost it, {my_faction} gained it, and I shall expect proper thanks in the minutes.

player_took_my_fief.text: {fief} has been taken by {player}. Well done, I suppose. I shall be sure to remember whose sword did the work.
{player} has taken {fief}. I had my reasons for not defending it, but I expect the council will want an explanation.
{player}, {fief} was mine, and you have taken it. Do not imagine I have forgotten.
{player}, a fine campaign for {fief}. I only wonder whether you intend to keep it, or merely hold it until the next vote.

encounter_alliance_yes.text: Agreed, {player}. We shall stand together against {enemy_faction}, and {rival} can find someone else to flatter.
Very well, {player}. I accept, but I shall be watching how you speak to {rival} and the council when they hear of it.
Yes, {player}. A pact against {enemy_faction} suits us both, and I have always preferred friends who sign their names.
I accept your offer, {player}. Let us keep this between our parties until the council has had its say.

encounter_alliance_no.text: No, {player}. I have heard how you deal with those who trust you. Go and find a lord who has not yet read the minutes.
I must decline, {player}. Not for lack of respect, but {rival} has already asked for the same favour and I cannot be seen to choose.
Not today, {player}. I like you well enough, but a pact now would make the council nervous, and I dislike nervous councils.

ambient_chatter.text: The roads out of {town} are muddy again. A good time to reconsider every promise made about the new bridge.
A small thing, but {village} is sending its tithe late again. I have written it down for the next session.
Lovely weather over {town} today. It will not last, but at least the council will be dry for its session.
I hear the ale in {village} is strong this season. Good for morale, if not for the minutes.
